glosses: The time when the Sun is below the horizon when the sky is dark.

examples.text: Most animals are awake at day and sleep at night.

The Bat—they called him the Bat. Like a bat he chose the night hours for his work of rapine; like a bat he struck and vanished, pouncingly, noiselessly; like a bat he never showed himself to the face of the day.

Irregular bedtimes may disrupt healthy brain development in young children, according to a study of intelligence and sleeping habits. ¶ Going to bed at a different time each night affected girls more than boys, but both fared worse on mental tasks than children who had a set bedtime, researchers found.

glosses: The period of darkness beginning at the end of evening astronomical twilight when the sun is 18 degrees below the horizon, and ending at the beginning of morning astronomical twilight.
A period of time often defined in the legal system as beginning 30 minutes after sunset, and ending 30 minutes before sunrise.
An evening or night spent at a particular activity.

examples.text: a night on the town

From the ground, Colombo’s port does not look like much. Those entering it are greeted by wire fences, walls dating back to colonial times and security posts. For mariners leaving the port after lonely nights on the high seas, the delights of the B52 Night Club and Stallion Pub lie a stumble away.

glosses: A day, or at least a night.

examples.text: I stayed my friend's house for three nights.

glosses: Nightfall.

examples.text: from noon till night

glosses: Darkness (due to it being nighttime).

examples.text: The cat disappeared into the night.

glosses: A dark blue colour, midnight blue.
A night's worth of competitions, generally one game.
Ellipsis of good night.

examples.text: Night, y'all! Thanks for a great evening!

glosses: To spend a night (in a place), to overnight.

examples.text: So I took seat and ate somewhat of my vivers, my horse also feeding upon his fodder, and we nighted in that spot and next morning I set out[.]

glosses: During the night following the current day; during the evening of today.

examples.text: I want to party tonight!
I had a wonderful time with you tonight.
I had a dreadful nightmare last night; I hope I sleep better tonight.

glosses: Last night.

examples.text:
Besides, I met Lord Bigot and Lord Salisbury,
With eyes as red as new-enkindled fire,
And others more, going to seek the grave
Of Arthur, whom they say is killed to-night
On your suggestion.

I dreamt tonight that I did feast with Caesar,
And things unluckily charge my fantasy;

glosses: The nighttime of the current day or date; this night.

examples.text: Tonight is the night.
I have high hopes for tonight.

glosses: Période qui s’écoule entre le coucher de soleil et le lever du soleil.
Période quotidienne durant laquelle le soleil est sous notre horizon et qu'il fait noir.

examples.text: Nous avions mis trois jours à l’œuvre, Varsovie n’eut besoin que d’une nuit, de la nuit du 29 novembre 1830 !
Pendant la nuit, cet Éden des malheureux, elle échappait aux ennuis, aux tracasseries qu’elle avait à supporter durant la journée.

Mme, M. et Mlle Chapoulot étaient éveillés, ne pouvaient plus se rendormir, et faisaient observer que la journée était assez longue pour répéter les musiques de théâtre, et que, dans une maison du Marais, on ne devait pas toucher du forté pendant la nuit…
La nuit vient de bonne heure au mois de février, et quand le futur beau-père et le futur gendre, qui étaient sortis ensemble du café, arrivèrent à la Madeleine, on allumait déjà les becs de gaz.
Le baromètre a baissé terriblement pendant la nuit et la matinée. Je m’attends à du gros temps.
«Qui utilise vraiment la nuit? 100% des chauves-souris, 90% des amphibiens et 60% des insectes», peut-on lire sur l'une des diapositives de la présentation de Daniel Gliedner.

glosses: Obscurité, ténèbres.

examples.text: […] La vision photopique est la vision de jour par opposition à la vision scotopique qui est la vision de nuit.
[…] dans la nuit, les pauvres arbres, sous l’effort du vent plus colère, gémissent et craquent.
[…] je vis tragiquement émerger de la nuit une étonnante masure en ruines à un étage, aux persiennes vermoulues et closes.
Je monte sur le pont et aperçois dans la nuit très noire les nombreuses lumières d’un vapeur qui s’éloigne.
D’une lucarne, dans le haut du mur, je voyais la nuit s’éclaircir. J’entendis un coq chanter […]
Il entra dans la grotte et se trouva alors dans une nuit profonde.

glosses: Symbole de destruction, d’oubli, de mort, de néant.

examples.text: La nuit éternelle.

examples.text: Bleu nuit.

glosses: Troisième personne du singulier de l’indicatif présent de nuire.

examples.text: La douleur n’est qu’un accident de ce mouvement vital ; loin de le favoriser, elle lui nuit au contraire ; elle retarde le rétablissement de l’ordre; elle favorise, comme nous allons le voir, les causes qui tendent à désalcaliser le sang.

glosses: The time when the Sun is above the horizon and it lights the sky.

examples.text: day and night;  I work at night and sleep during the day.

The day was cool and snappy for August, and the Rise all green with a lavish nature. Now we plunged into a deep shade with the boughs lacing each other overhead, and crossed dainty, rustic bridges over the cold trout-streams,[…].

glosses: A period of time equal or almost equal to a full day-night cycle, being 24 hours long.

I've been here for two days and a bit.

glosses: A period of time equal or almost equal to a full day-night cycle, being 24 hours long.
The time taken for the Sun to seem to be in the same place in the sky twice; a solar day.
A period of time equal or almost equal to a full day-night cycle, being 24 hours long.
The time taken for the Earth to make a full rotation about its axis with respect to the fixed stars; a sidereal day or stellar day.
A 24-hour period beginning at 6am or sunrise.

examples.text: Your 8am forecast: The high for the day will be 30 and the low, before dawn, will be 10.

glosses: A period of time between two set times which mark the beginning and the end of day in a calendar, such as from midnight to the following midnight or (Judaism) from nightfall to the following nightfall.

examples.text: Monday is the first day of the week in many countries of the world.
The day begins at midnight.

glosses: The rotational period of a planet.

examples.text: A day on Mars is slightly over 24 hours.

glosses: The part of a day period which one spends at one’s job, school, etc.

examples.text: I worked two days last week.

“[…]if you call my duds a ‘livery’ again there'll be trouble. It's bad enough to go around togged out like a life saver on a drill day, but I can stand that 'cause I'm paid for it. What I won't stand is to have them togs called a livery.[…]”

glosses: An observance lasting for a day, such as an annual holiday.

examples.text: Christmas Day
Remembrance Day

glosses: A specified time or period; time, considered with reference to the existence or prominence of a person or thing; age; time; era.

examples.text: every dog has its day; in that day; back in the day; in those days

This new-comer was a man who in any company would have seemed striking.[…]Indeed, all his features were in large mold, like the man himself, as though he had come from a day when skin garments made the proper garb of men.
If they had no more food than they had had in Jones's day, at least they did not have less.

In his senior year, he had run across an old '66 Chevy Super Sport headed for the junkyard, bought it for a song, and overhauled it with his dad's help, turning it into the big red muscle car it was back in its day.

glosses: A period of contention of a day or less.

examples.text: The day belonged to the Allies.

glosses: To spend a day (in a place).

examples.text: I nighted and dayed in Damascus town[.]

translations.source_sense_description: landschaftlich mundartlich: am derzeitigen, gegenwärtigen Tag (der gerade abläuft)

glosses: On the current day or date.

examples.text: I want this done today.
Today, my brother went to the shops.

glosses: In the current era; nowadays; these days.

examples.text: In the 1500s, people had to do things by hand, but today we have electric can openers.

Private-equity nabobs bristle at being dubbed mere financiers.[…]Much of their pleading is public-relations bluster. Clever financial ploys are what have made billionaires of the industry’s veterans. “Operational improvement” in a portfolio company has often meant little more than promising colossal bonuses to sitting chief executives if they meet ambitious growth targets. That model is still prevalent today.

glosses: The day of a recurring cycle or event which is currently happening.

examples.text: We used to prepare everything today, but now we split it over two days.

glosses: The current day or date.

examples.text: Today is the day we'll fix this once and for all.
We could've spent today at the seaside if it weren't gusty.
Yesterday, upon the stair / I met a man who wasn’t there / He wasn’t there again today / I wish, I wish he’d go away …

glosses: The 24-hour period beginning at 5am or 6am or sunrise of the current day.
The present era; nowadays.

examples.text: This is the sporty jacket for today's modern man on the go.
The youth of today have never known what life is like without a cell phone.

glosses: Current; up to date.

examples.text: Actually, it's more like the blues. It's pop blues. I feel it's very American. It's very today. It's what people respond to today.
[…] she (Françoise Hardy) is so today, so white boots and yé-yé, that she can make anyone over 25 (me) feel prehistoric, raccoon coat and rah-rah.

translations.source_sense_description: landschaftlich mundartlich: am derzeitigen, gegenwärtigen Tag (der gerade abläuft)

glosses: À la date présente, ce jour même.

examples.text: Il arrive aujourd’hui à midi.
Hâtons-nous aujourd’hui de jouir de la vie.

glosses: À présent, à l'époque où l'on vit.

examples.text: […] jadis, on croyait que la férule était l’outil le plus nécessaire pour le maître d’école ; aujourd’hui, les peines corporelles ont disparu de notre enseignement public.
À l’abri du monopole et de la paix qui en résultait, les Groenlandais se multiplièrent et aujourd’hui, deux cents ans après l’arrivée de Hans Egede, ils sont au nombre de 15.000 […]
Encore aujourd’hui, le diocèse de Rodez est, de tous, celui qui fournit le plus grand nombre de prêtres, le plus grand nombre de missionnaires.
À partir du mois de juin, la plage, aujourd’hui disparue, se couvrait de tentes pour la saison des bains de mer.
Sans toi, les émotions d’aujourd’hui ne seraient que la peau morte des émotions d’autrefois.
En ce temps-là, la vieillesse était une dignité ; aujourd’hui, elle est une charge.

glosses: Date quelconque par rapport à une autre qui en est très proche.
target_senses.note: Dans ce sens, on l’oppose ordinairement à demain ou à hier

examples.text: Aujourd’hui, elle veut une chose, demain elle en voudra une autre.
Aujourd'hui, maman est morte. Ou peut-être hier, je ne sais pas. — (Albert Camus, L'Étranger, Les classiques des sciences sociales, 2015.)
Ce qui fut bien hier peut-il être mal aujourd’hui ?

glosses: Présent, temps présent, contemporanéité.

examples.text: Vivons pleinement l’aujourd’hui.

Le vierge, le vivace et le bel aujourd’hui
Va-t-il nous déchirer avec un coup d’aile ivre
Ce lac dur oublié que hante sous le givre
Le transparent glacier des vols qui n’ont pas fui !
Il n’y a pas d’aujourd’hui, il n’y a que la douceur des jours passés et un lendemain incertain.
